what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat fungal (yeast-like) infections of the skin, hair, and nails. It works by stopping the fungus from growing. It is commonly used for infections like ringworm, athlete's foot, jock itch, and fungal nail infections. It does NOT work for infections caused by bacteria or viruses.
how_to_take: Take this tablet by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. It is best to take it with a meal that contains some fat, such as a meal with milk, butter, or peanut butter. This helps your body absorb the medicine better and may also help reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do NOT skip doses, even if you start feeling better — finish the full course of treatment.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on the type and location of your infection, your weight, and your overall health. Common adult doses range from 375 mg to 750 mg per day, taken as a single dose or split into smaller doses. Children's doses are based on body weight. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use this medicine after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine. Alcohol can cause serious reactions including flushing, fast heartbeat, and nausea. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause dizziness or confusion in some people. Avoid prolonged sun exposure, tanning beds, and sunlamps — this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Use sunscreen and protective clothing when going outdoors. Avoid taking antacids or other medications without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, as some medicines can interact with griseofulvin.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: severe skin rash, hives, or blistering; swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of an allergic reaction); yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or pale stools (signs of liver problems); unusual bruising or bleeding; severe dizziness or confusion; numbness or tingling in your hands or feet; signs of a serious skin reaction such as painful red or peeling skin; or if your infection does not seem to be improving after several weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: This medicine works slowly. You may not notice improvement right away. Skin infections (like ringworm or athlete's foot) may improve within 2 to 4 weeks, but treatment may last several weeks. Scalp infections (tinea capitis) may require 4 to 6 weeks of treatment. Nail infections take much longer — fingernail infections may need 4 to 6 months of treatment, and toenail infections may need 6 months or longer. It is very important to complete the full course of treatment even if your symptoms go away, to make sure the infection is fully cleared.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medicine should NOT be used during pregnancy. It may cause harm to an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least one month after finishing this medicine. Men should also use birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after finishing. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medicine. Children: This medicine can be used in children, but the dose will be carefully calculated based on body weight. Do not give this medicine to infants without a doctor's guidance. Elderly: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects. Use with caution and follow your doctor's instructions carefully. Liver disease: This medicine should be used with great caution — or not at all — in people with liver problems. Tell your doctor if you have any history of liver disease.
